 Order

Appellant/Insurance company has filed this appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act assailing the award dated 10/12/2021 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Morena on the ground of liability; a s liability for payment of compensation amount has been fastened over the appellant- Insurance Company.

entities.text:
Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Facts giving rise to the controversy in brief are that respondents No. 1 to 3/claimants have filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles act claiming a compensation of Rs. 77,25,000/-
for the death of husband of respondent/claimant No.1 and father of respondens / claimants No. 2 and 3 namely Gurcharan Lal Sharma.

It was alleged that on the fateful day of 8/7/2014 to attend a marriage programme deceased alongwith his friend/respondent No. 4 Abhishek Kumar Shukla were going in a Car bearing registration No. UP78DM1603 to Dholpur via Morena.

Respondent No. 4 was driving the car in a rash and negligent manner and when it reached near Baba Ki Tekri, vllage Bareh, it dashed a tractor trolley from back, due to which deceased Gurcharan Lal Sharma died.

Therefore, a claim petition was filed and learned Claims Tribunal after appreciating the evidence available before it awarded a sum of Rs. 12,47,320/- for the death of Gurcharan Lal Sharmaa as compensation and appellant/Insurance Company was held liable for payment of compensation.
The aforesaid fastening of liability of payment of compensation amount, has been challenged by Insurance Company by filing this appeal.
I t is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that though evidence has come on record that due to negligent driving of car driver the accident happened however police has not registered any case against the car driver and no charge-sheet against him has been filed
; however, Insurance Company of Car has been held liable for payment of compensation amount.
The interest as awarded by Claims Tribunal @ of 9% is also on higher side.
Further the driver and owner of the Tractor were not made party to the lis.

and the amount under the head loss of consortium as awarded by the Claim Tribunal is against the settled principles of law as has been held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017 ACJ 2700).

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017 ACJ 2700)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants argued in support of the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
This appeal is preferred by the appellant/Insurance company.
The deceased was travelling in the car alongwith his family.
the Car collided with a tractor in middle of the road, as a result of which, the deceased Gurucharan Lal Sharma succumbed to the injuries sustained by him.

sentences.text: The report of the accident was lodged by brother of respondent no. 4, who was driver and owner of the car.
Since, the driver of the tractor has already been died, therefore, police filed the FR in the matter.

It is not disputed that in the claim petition, owner and insurance company of the tractor were not made party and the application of the Insurance Company of Car for impleading the owner and insurance company of the tractor got rejected by the Tribunal vide order dated 19/4/2018.

It is also not in dispute that neither any report has been registered nor charge-sheet has been filed against the car driver but in the statement of respondent No. 1/claimant who is widow of deceased Gurucharan Lal Sharma it has clearly surfaced that due to negligent driving of the car driver, the incident has occurred.
Statement of the respondent no. 1 remained intact and controverted in cross-examination and no evidence has been produced in rebuttal of the same.

The car driver has not come to witness box and therefore, statement of the respondent No. 1 said to be quite reliable; therefore, in the opinion of this Court there being no police report or charge-sheet against the car driver is not material as the same is not neccesary for claiming compensation.
Further the Tribunal has held both car driver and tractor driver responsible for the accident and said finding deserves to be upheld and maintained in view of the evidence that has come on record.

Further in light of the decision of Apex Court in the matter of Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and Ores., 2015 ACJ 1441, the appellant/Insurance Company is free to initiate separate proceedings for recovery of compensation amount, if any, towards contributory negligence against the owner and Insurance Company of Tractor.

entities.text: Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and Ores., 2015 ACJ 1441
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As regards, the amount awarded by Claims Tribunal under the head loss of consortium, in the opinion of this Court, Claims Tribunal erred in award the same in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of Pranay Sethi (supra) in which only Rs. 70,000/- has been awarded towards conventional heads, namely, loss to estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses and therefore,
since, the Claims Tribunal has awarded total sum of Rs. 88,000/- towards loss of parental consortium to each of 2 children, in the opinion of this Court same is not sustainable in the eyes of law and therefore, same is liable to be deducted.

As regards interest rate, in the opinion of this Court award of interest at the rate of 9% per annum is also on higher side looking to the decision of Apex Court in the matter of Divisional; Manager, Oriental Insurance co. Ltd., Cuttack Vs. Kalbalatha Mohaapatra, 2005 (1) TAC 569, wherein it has been held that rate of interest must be just and reasonable depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case taking all relevant factos including inflation, change of economy and policy adopted by Reserve Bank of India and accordingly same is reduged from 9% to 7%.

entities.text: Manager, Oriental Insurance co. Ltd., Cuttack Vs. Kalbalatha Mohaapatra, 2005 (1) TAC 569
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I n the result, the appeal is allowed in part and impugned award is modified to the extent that now respondents No. 2 and 3/claimants shall not be entitled for any amount under the head loss of consortium and the award amount shall carry interest @ of 7% per annum instead of 9% per annum.
`Rest of the conditions shall remain intact.
Appeal stands allowed in part and disposed of with above modification in impugned award.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
